```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidyquant)
library(knitr)
```

## Data

The data set is from Federal Reserve Economic Data and is a time series on the unemployment rate. It includes data for the United States at large, as well as for Texas, California, New York, and Oregon. It runs from 1976 -2026 and has observations monthly.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#Load Data
unemp_raw = read_rds("data/unemp_raw.rds")

##Clean Data
unemp <- unemp_raw |>
  rename(unemployment_rate = price) |>
  mutate(
    region = case_when(
      symbol == "UNRATE" ~ "United States",
      symbol == "ORUR"    ~ "Oregon",
      symbol == "CAUR" ~ "California",
      symbol == "TXUR" ~ "Texas",
      symbol == "NYUR" ~ "New York"
    )
  )
unemp <- unemp |>
  arrange(region, date) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  mutate(
    unemployment_rate = replace(
      unemployment_rate,
      date == as.Date("2025-10-01"),
      unemployment_rate[date == as.Date("2025-09-01")]
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()
head(unemp)
```

## Wrangling

```{r}
#| echo: false
#Summaries
unemp <- unemp |>
  arrange(region, date) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  mutate(unemployment_rate_change = unemployment_rate - lag(unemployment_rate)) |>
  ungroup()

unemp_recent <- unemp |>
  filter(date >= "2015-01-01")

unemp_summary <- unemp |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarize(
    mean_rate = mean(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_rate  = min(unemployment_rate,  na.rm = TRUE),
    max_rate  = max(unemployment_rate,  na.rm = TRUE)
  )

unemp_recent_summary <- unemp_recent |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarize(
    mean_rate = mean(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_rate  = min(unemployment_rate,  na.rm = TRUE),
    max_rate  = max(unemployment_rate,  na.rm = TRUE)
  )
#Extremes 
unemp_top_increases <- unemp |>
  slice_max(order_by = unemployment_rate_change, n=5)

unemp_top_decreases <- unemp |>
  slice_min(order_by = unemployment_rate_change, n=5)

unemp_top_increases_no_covid <- unemp |>
  filter_out(date >= "2020-01-01" & date<= "2020-12-31")|>
  slice_max(order_by = unemployment_rate_change, n=5)

unemp_top_decreases_no_covid <- unemp |>
  filter_out(date >= "2020-01-01" & date<= "2020-12-31")|>
  slice_min(order_by = unemployment_rate_change, n=5)

#Tables
summary_table <-kable(
  head(unemp_summary),
  digits    = 3,                                   # round numbers
  col.names = c("Region", "Mean Unemployment Rate", "Minimum Unemployment Rate", "Maximum Unemployment Rate"),
  caption   = "Unemployment Rate Summary",
  align     = "lccc",                              # one letter per column: l/c/r
  row.names = TRUE
)

recent_summary_table <-kable(
  head(unemp_recent_summary),
  digits    = 3,                                   # round numbers
  col.names = c("Region", "Mean Recent Unemployment Rate", "Minimum Recent Unemployment Rate", "Maximum Recent Unemployment Rate"),
  caption   = "Recent Unemployment Rate Summary",
  align     = "lccc",                              # one letter per column: l/c/r
  row.names = TRUE
)

decreases_table <-kable(
  head(unemp_top_decreases_no_covid[2:5]),
  digits    = 3,                                   
  col.names = c("Date", "Unemployment Rate", "Region","Unemployment Rate Change"),
  caption   = "Top Decrases in unemployment (Excluding 2020)",
  align     = "lccc",                            
  row.names = TRUE
)

increases_table <-kable(
  head(unemp_top_increases_no_covid[2:5]),
  digits    = 3,                                   
  col.names = c("Date", "Unemployment Rate", "Region","Unemployment Rate Change"),
  caption   = "Top Increases in unemployment (Excluding 2020)",
  align     = "lccc",                              
  row.names = TRUE
)

print(summary_table)
print(recent_summary_table)
print(decreases_table)
print(increases_table)
```

## Visualization

```{r}
#| echo: false
#Line plots
ggplot(unemp, aes(x=date,y=unemployment_rate, color= region))+
  labs(x="Time",y="Unemployment Rate (percent)", title = "Unemployment Rate Over Time")+
  geom_line()+
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(unemp, aes(x=date,y=unemployment_rate))+
  labs(title = "Unemployment Rate by Region Over Time",y="Unemployment Rate (percent)",x="Time")+
  geom_line()+
  facet_wrap(~ region,ncol=1)+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(4, 16, by = 4),
                     labels = scales::label_number(suffix = "%"))+
  theme_minimal()

#Bar Chart
ggplot(unemp_summary, aes(x=fct_reorder(region, mean_rate),y=mean_rate))+
  geom_col()+
  labs(title = "Average Unemployment by Region", x="Region",y="Unemployment Rate (percent)")+
  theme_minimal()

##Change in unemployment over time
ggplot(unemp|>filter_out(date >= "2013-01-01"| date <= "2005-01-01"),
       aes(x=date,y=unemployment_rate_change, color= region))+
  labs(x="Time",y="Unemployment Rate Change (percent)",
       title = "Unemployment Rate Change, Great Recession")+
  facet_wrap(~ region,ncol=1)+
  geom_line()+
  theme_minimal()

```

Here I'm plotting change in unemployment rate over the period shortly before, during, and after the great recession. I chose this because I wanted to see how different states, which intuitively have jobs distributed across sectors differently, were affected by the crisis.
